simple.meaning: מֹשֶׁל (môshel) is a Hebrew word meaning “empire ; a parallel.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: מֹשֶׁל (H4915) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Job 41:25, with occurrences in Job, Daniel, Zechariah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מֹשֶׁל (H4915) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in מֹשֶׁל (H4915) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: מֹשֶׁל (môshel) / H4915 is traced through Job 41:25, Daniel 11:4, Zechariah 9:10 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H4915. moshel I. [ מָ֫שֶׁל noun [masculine] likeness, one like ; only suffix מָשְׁלוֺ Job 41:25 his likeness , i.e. one like him. II. [ מ֫שֶׁל ] noun [masculine] dominion ; — suffix עַדיָֿםמָשְׁלוֺמִיָּם Zech 9:10 (of Messianic king); מָשָׁ֑ל אֲשֶׁר כְּמָשְׁלוֺ Dan 11:4 (of Alexander).
